title: Report Actual Misuse at IdentityTheft.gov
body_md:
Exposure of data does not by itself mean misuse has occurred. If you do find that exposed information has been used — an account you did not open, a tax return already filed in your name, charges or medical claims you do not recognize — report it at IdentityTheft.gov, the federal government's central resource for identity theft recovery.

1. Go to IdentityTheft.gov and describe the type of misuse. The site produces a personal recovery plan with steps ordered for your situation.
2. Completing the report generates an FTC Identity Theft Report and pre-filled letters for credit bureaus, businesses, and debt collectors.
3. Assistance is also available by phone at 1-877-438-4338.
4. Keep copies of the report and every letter; credit bureaus and businesses may request them when removing fraudulent accounts or charges.
5. Return to the site as you complete steps; the recovery plan tracks progress and updates the checklist.

Use this module once misuse actually appears in a credit report, statement, benefits document, or collection notice identified through the review steps above.
